subject: Math
prompt: A store sells two types of shirts, Type X and Type Y. Of all the shirts in the store, $40%$ are Type X shirts. Of all the Type X shirts, $30%$ are on sale. What percentage of all shirts in the store are Type X shirts on sale?
explanation: It's given that $40\%$ of all shirts are Type X. It's also given that of all Type X shirts, $30\%$ are on sale. To find what percentage of all shirts are Type X shirts on sale, calculate $30\%$ of $40\%$: $(0.30)(0.40) = 0.12$, which equals $12\%$.
